fact: La Razon (2026-06-05) states ACE has been operative in Equatorial Guinea since December 2012 and is the country's one in-service submarine cable, with Medusa to be the second.

AFR-IX (2018-06-06) states Ceiba-2, a 400 km cable linking Malabo, Bata and Kribi (Cameroon), was inaugurated on 4 June 2018 as the first direct international fibre link, alongside the ACE cable: two routes in service.
source_slug: 2018-06-06 Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon are now more connected - AFR-IX telecom

fact: The ACE consortium states the cable entered service on 15 December 2012 and is the first international submarine cable to land in Equatorial Guinea, at Bata.

AidData record of the China Eximbank loan states the Ceiba-2 cable, a 400 km submarine system owned and operated by GITGE connecting Malabo and Bata with a branching unit to Kribi in Cameroon, was built under the loan (status Completed, end year 2017).

The same record states the Ceiba-2 and ACE submarine stations in Bata sit next to each other and are directly fibre-linked, so GNQ has both ACE and Ceiba-2 at Bata; same station, so two not independent.

GITGE's annual report states it supplies capacity to ISPs in GNQ and guarantees equal access under open, non-discriminatory access, selling only to providers and government companies; content is internally dated about 2016, upload path 2025-07.

SPIN states that on 10 November 2025 the Gabonese and Equatorial Guinean national fibre backbones were inaugurated as physically and logically interconnected at Meyo-Kyé/Ebebeyin, with tests confirming stable traffic exchange Bitam-Ebebeyin and Libreville-Bata, ensuring continuity of international traffic.
